items.title: Introducing Krea 3
items.excerpt: Krea released Krea 3, a new image editing model. Most edits finish in under 8 seconds at native 2K for $0.06 an image, take up to 6 reference images, and keep products and characters consistent from one image to the next. It is live for Krea's 30M users and through fal, Replicate and OpenRouter.

items.title: Design together with code layers on the canvas
items.excerpt: Code layers is now in open beta. Teams can build code-backed prototypes on the Figma canvas, starting from GitHub, a local folder, a prototype brought in through the Figma MCP server, or a live site captured with the Chrome extension, and then compare variations side by side.

items.title: Build by design: New workflows for new ways of building
items.excerpt: Dylan Field's Config India recap sets out Figma's 'building to think vs building to ship' framing and covers code layers, design systems for agents, Specs and Payload, all aimed at bringing teams, agents, design, code and context onto one full-stack canvas.

items.title: Cloud Agent Canvases and Environment Improvements
items.excerpt: Cursor's cloud agents can now build interactive canvases as part of their work and share them with a team by link. An Environments API also entered beta, with support for up to 300 repos per environment.

items.title: Vercel Ship 2026 recap
items.excerpt: Vercel's Ship recap includes SAP rebuilding its design system to be composable so that people and agents assemble interfaces from the same parts with v0 and json-render, ZoomInfo embedding v0 for 40,000+ customers, and Notion's Ivan Zhao telling designers to 'design the API first and the UI last'.

items.title: I used Nvidia RTX Spark's AI agent to run Blender – here's what happened
items.excerpt: A hands-on test of the on-device AI agent on Nvidia's RTX Spark laptops, asking it to drive Blender tasks. It reports where agentic control of a 3D app works and where it still falls short for a working artist.

items.title: No amount of renaming can fix AI's growing reputation problem
items.excerpt: Creative Bloq argues that Elon Musk's attempts to rebrand 'AI slop' point to a deeper reputation problem for generative imagery among creatives and audiences.

items.title: A week with RTX Spark: everything we've learned using Nvidia's new laptops
items.excerpt: The Verge spent a week with Nvidia's RTX Spark Windows-on-Arm laptops from Asus, HP and Lenovo, testing the 'superchip' pitched for local AI and creative workloads.

items.title: Is Your Organization Messing Up AI Adoption?
items.excerpt: Paul Boag goes back to his book Digital Adaptation to show how lessons from digital transformation apply to rolling out AI across organizations and design teams.

items.title: Welcome Muse Spark Open: open-weight frontier multimodal mixture-of-experts model from Meta
items.excerpt: Meta released Muse Spark Open, an open-weight multimodal mixture-of-experts model, on Hugging Face. It can be run and fine-tuned locally, including on Macs through MLX.

items.title: Human in the loop means making sure the human is not out of the loop
items.excerpt: Agents now act before we ask and reach past what we authorized. Patrick Neeman argues that a person in the loop is not enough if nobody owns the outcome, and lists what designers should consider when designing agent experiences.

items.title: The AI experience doesn't care about your org chart
items.excerpt: AI is pulling content design, enterprise content strategy, knowledge management and model behavior into a single user experience. Kate Agena argues that design teams' ways of working have not caught up.

items.title: Nobody wants your AI app
items.excerpt: Dan Maccarone argues that buyers want AI to disappear into the platforms they already use, not to arrive as yet another standalone app, and says this changes what product designers should build.

items.title: Meta, Milan's Pinacoteca di Brera, and EssilorLuxottica Expand Access to Art Through AI Glasses
items.excerpt: Meta, the Pinacoteca di Brera and EssilorLuxottica launched 'Sensing Art', a pilot that uses Meta AI glasses to describe and interpret masterpieces for visitors, an accessibility-first spatial experience built on AI glasses.

items.title: Astra Studios Launches AstraLabs, Teams with VerSe on AI Pipeline
items.excerpt: Astra Studios and VerSe will co-develop an AI-native production pipeline on SparkStation. It carries a production from script to distribution and keeps faces, wardrobe and locations consistent across shots.

items.title: AI News: 6 New Models & A Nano Banana Killer
items.excerpt: Matt Wolfe's weekly roundup leads with Krea 3 making image editing 'seriously easy', then hands-on tests of Gemini 4 Argon and Meta's Muse Wonder, new open-weight models and the latest OpenAI updates.

items.title: Getting started with Code Layers | Figma
items.excerpt: Figma designer advocate Anthony DiSpezio shows code layers in open beta: starting from a codebase, exploring variations with the agent, extracting designs into editable layers, and pushing changes to a GitHub branch for review.

items.title: Meta and Apple team up to make Muse AI models run better on Macs
items.excerpt: Meta and Apple are working together to optimize Meta's open Muse Spark model for Apple silicon through MLX, so the multimodal model runs locally on Macs.
